- Static date preconditions accept only valid HTTP dates, including obsolete date forms and their rolling two-digit year boundary. ISO and free-form dates are ignored.

- Static files with future or pre-1900 modification times omit Last-Modified and use ETags for revalidation, so a skewed build cannot supply an invalid date validator.

- `sendCoalesced` contains reentrant sends from `toJSON`, discards superseded frames before sending, and retains newer queued values when a send encounters backpressure.

- `sendCoalesced` rejects invalid topic and event names before queueing, even on a backpressured socket, and preserves an existing value for the same key. Envelope construction failures are contained when the queue drains.

- `sendCoalesced` drops and reports every thrown serialization value, including strings and null, instead of embedding thrown strings as malformed JSON. Values flushed immediately still throw to their caller.

- Test-server wire broadcasts no longer inflate close-hook traffic counters; directed sends and wire-id announcements remain counted, including with outbound fault injection.

- Clarify that trusted server subscription APIs accept system topics through the app hook without a namespace escape option; client wire subscriptions keep their existing guard.

- Close hooks receive an empty subscription Set when a connection's subscription registry is corrupt, preserving safe teardown on production, testing and Vite.

- The raw subscription-accounting control removes its deliberately uncharged membership before closing, so it leaves the worker counters balanced.

- Synthetic subscription-registry tests isolate their accounting callback, preserving real server counters when the suites run together.

- Vite subscriber iteration passes the adapter socket and its user data to callbacks, so matching subscribers can be inspected and sent messages without throwing.

- `releaseSubscription` in the subscriptions subpath removes failed framework admissions, including derived and publish access, while independently pending authorizations can still complete. Explicit unsubscribe continues to cancel pending attempts.

- Pending hook-installed subscriptions no longer count as completed server grants. Server re-grants authorize the membership before acknowledging it, and wire, observer and resume gates reject unconfirmed membership.

- A revoked subscribe cannot disclose recover history through membership installed by its own hook. Single and batch recover paths retain legitimate server re-grants.

- The test server checks the final subscribe gate before recording a grant, matching production and development when authorization changes during an async hook.

- The export type gate rejects JavaScript subpaths without declarations and
  follows runtime and declaration star re-exports, including cycles and
  ambiguous names, instead of silently skipping those public surfaces.

- Self-initiated client socket closes report `disconnected` immediately, even
  while the browser's close event is pending. `send()` returns true for local
  admission and false for a disconnected or paused socket; serialization and
  transport exceptions propagate. Late callbacks cannot overwrite a replacement
  connection's state or subscription retries.


- **Vite upgrade lifetime.** The real HTTP upgrade listener routes by the raw
  target, refuses malformed targets and path aliases with 400, and owns socket
  errors before awaiting handler loading or the application hook. Disconnects
  stop admission after either await; the event callback contains other failures
  to that socket. Raw TCP and TLS tests verify refusals followed by successful
  upgrades, and TCP resets during both asynchronous waits leave the server serving.
- **Vite authentication request bodies.** The hook receives a bounded request
  stream without waiting for body completion. Declared lengths over 64 KiB are
  rejected before invocation; consumed bytes past the cap raise the same
  `PayloadTooLargeError` as production. Ignored remainders are drained after the
  answer so HTTP/2 streams can complete. Real built-runtime and Vite tests pin
  ignored chunked and stalled bodies, exact-cap reads, over-cap reads, HTTP/2
  completion, and disconnects before and during a body read.
- Documentation-map checks analyze self-contained appended HTML fixtures
  without repeating the unchanged README ownership walk. Full-document checks
  retain coverage of parser context while root attributes, executable markup
  and navigation cases use the ordinary test deadline.

- **Authentication body reads settle when the client disconnects.** The auth
  route invokes the body's failure callback from its abort handler, matching
  the SSR and admin routes. Real TCP resets cover declared-length and chunked
  text, JSON and form reads, hook rejection, and return of pooled request state.

- The bundled client's auth POST sends `x-requested-with: XMLHttpRequest`,
  matching the existing origin guard. A real client and built runtime pin
  successful preflight and WebSocket connection without `Origin` or
  `Sec-Fetch-Site`; the server still refuses a missing or unrecognized header
  when no other configured origin signal accepts the request.
- Auth rate-limit refusals round the configured window up before adding
  `Retry-After` jitter. Built-runtime HTTP tests cover fractional windows and
  retain the default whole-second range; rate accounting itself is unchanged.

- The Vite plugin resolves `envPrefix` from the adapter metadata before
  reading its `ORIGIN` pin, including direct `sveltekit(config)` setups and
  the older config-file fallback. Real dev HTTP and WebSocket requests cover
  the prefixed pin and a conflicting bare variable, including the
  authentication hook's request URL and both same-origin gates.
- A prefixed built fixture now exercises the proxy warning and SSR
  `ADDRESS_HEADER` / `XFF_DEPTH` diagnostics. The real-runtime test helper
  applies, scrubs, compares and restores that variant's prefixed environment
  while callers keep unprefixed names; real requests verify inherited body
  limits are scrubbed and unrelated bare variables remain unchanged.

- **The handshake case-folding regression reaches the character comparison.**
  Its Kelvin-sign input has the same length as `websocket` and is explicitly
  shown to lowercase to that token, so a Unicode-folding implementation fails.

- **sendWireBatch validates encoded payloads before allocating a wire id.**
  `src/runtime/handler/platform.js` and `src/testing.js` reject non-nullish
  results other than `Uint8Array` on the batch and per-entry paths. The check
  accepts byte-array views across realms and `Buffer` without copying them.
  Invalid results throw `TypeError`; codec exceptions, nullish fallback and
  valid delivery keep their existing behavior. The isolated real-socket cases
  in `test/send-wire-batch-payload.test.js` exercise both runtimes and check
  the delivered binding, payload bytes, partial delivery and refusal boundary.

- **Wire send and publish paths validate codec results before binary admission.**
  `sendWire`, both stateful `publishWire` branches, the shared stateless encode
  helper and stateful batch/per-entry delivery reject non-nullish results that
  are not `Uint8Array` values before allocating a wire id or building a frame.
  The production and testing paths use native brand checks without copying
  payloads. Real-socket tests cover all eight send/publish branches, original
  exceptions, nullish fallback and deliveries completed before a later failure.


- **Presence updates with an empty folded identity name:** the default guard
  compares the exact configured key when lowercasing and retaining only ASCII
  letters and digits leaves an empty name. A key such as `用户` no longer
  reserves unrelated Unicode-only or punctuation-only fields. Nonempty folds
  retain their existing aliases, including Unicode letters that lowercase to
  ASCII, and the fold is computed once per tracker. Reserved-field warnings
  distinguish the exact empty-fold key from unrelated names. Other sensitive
  and structural guards and the explicit client allowlist remain unchanged.
  Real WebSocket tests cover delivered diffs and fresh snapshots, Unicode case
  distinctions, punctuation-only keys, non-ASCII aliases with a nonempty fold,
  warning eligibility, and default and explicit client update permissions.

- **HTTP/1.1 on nginx page routes:** the catch-all example explicitly sets
  `proxy_http_version 1.1` and clears the upstream `Connection` header. The
  text states that uWS answers HTTP/1.0 with 505 and links nginx's documented
  change from an HTTP/1.0 default before 1.29.7. A real production fixture
  answered raw HTTP/1.0 with 505 and HTTP/1.1 with 200.
- **Cookie-refresh attribution:** both handshake-cookie explanations now
  describe the deployed client and intermediary dependency without naming a
  vendor as the cause of a failed handshake. The HTTP `authenticate` path
  remains recommended, and its implementation and build-time warning are
  unchanged. The protocol reference permits cookies on the handshake.
- **Measured control-egress examples:** README and control-budget comments no
  longer call a numeric-reference overflow batch the worst case. On the lead
  runtime, an 8,191-byte frame with ref 1 delivered 2,496 replies totaling
  177,042 payload bytes (21.6x); a 128-character ASCII ref delivered 2,453
  replies totaling 490,383 bytes (59.9x). Longer refs can amplify further.
  Counts exclude welcome and transport framing; the 4 MiB per 10-second
  ceiling and close code 4429 do not change.

- **Publish and send return contracts describe local outcomes.** Corrected
  `platform.send`'s reversed 0/1 status names and `platform.publish`'s delivery
  wording in the declarations. `docs/architecture.md` records the decision
  against a separate asynchronous receipt API and distinguishes native local
  status, worker relay scheduling, and application acknowledgements. Runtime
  behavior and signatures are unchanged.

- **Bodyless HTTP lengths are validated before reaching uWS.** `endBodyless`
  accepts only non-negative safe integers from its existing decimal-prefix
  parser, preserving `42abc` as 42. Invalid lengths are omitted on 304 and
  HEAD. The auth and SSR writers reject invalid final Response statuses before
  writing application headers or cookies. Raw HTTP tests cover both writers,
  HEAD with and without an application body, boundary lengths, and status 0.

- **Immutable static assets evaluate request preconditions.** Existence
  wildcards work without an emitted ETag, in the same precedence order as
  mutable assets; empty list elements cannot match an absent validator. Real
  GET and HEAD requests cover identity, brotli and gzip, conditional metadata,
  unchanged normal responses, precedence and missing date validators.


- **Hook containment survives a throwing console logger.** The message and
  lifecycle failure paths guard their diagnostic calls independently of closing
  the connection. Real built-runtime, test-server and dev-server regressions
  exercise synchronous throws and rejected hooks with a failing logger; the
  built drain case uses actual socket backpressure. A real control flood also
  verifies the existing protected diagnostic path still closes with 4429 when
  both warning and error logging throw.

- Request-lane readiness tests use an isolated fixture lifecycle so serial suites cannot inherit a previously closed runtime.

- Extra-entry chunk matching resolves real paths on both sides, with an
  absolute-path fallback for virtual or unreadable IDs. A real Rollup build
  through a directory junction proves sanitized, colliding names all execute
  in startup order.
- On Windows, an encoded GET or HEAD containing a reserved filesystem
  character may serve an exact in-memory static index entry. The exception
  follows reserved mount checks and precedes prerendered routing; unindexed
  short names and alternate streams still receive 400. Real HTTP checks cover
  Unicode tilde names, encoded tildes, HEAD, methods and reserved admin paths.
- Prerendered clean paths receive collision-safe composed aliases together
  with directory-style redirect metadata. A later real name removes any
  generated alias and its slash policy. Real disk indexing and HTTP requests
  cover file and directory output, base roots, both collision orders and
  normalization to plain ASCII.
- **`vite dev` accepts `server.https` requests as production does.** The
  auth and upgrade origin checks pass `isTls` from `req.socket.encrypted`;
  they passed `false`, so under `server.https`, where Vite terminates TLS as
  production does under SSL_CERT, the same-origin rule expected an `http://`
  Origin and refused the browser's. `http1Headers` (src/vite.js) drops the
  pseudo-headers node's http2 compatibility layer leaves in `req.headers` and
  takes `host` from `:authority`, as SvelteKit's `getRequest` does; the auth
  and dashboard middlewares read their headers through it. Answering over
  HTTP/2, the auth lane leaves out of the hook's Response the
  connection-specific headers HTTP/2 does not carry
  (`connectionSpecificHeader`), on most of which node's http2 layer throws
  when the response is written; over HTTP/1.1 they are written. Header
  values and cookies with text past ASCII go to node as their UTF-8 bytes
  (`wireValue`), which is what uWS writes; node takes one byte per
  character, refusing one past U+00FF over HTTP/1.1 and keeping only its low
  byte over HTTP/2.

- **`vite dev`'s auth lane writes a hook Response as production does, or
  answers 500 with nothing of the hook's on it.** Before it sets anything,
  the lane refuses a status that is not an integer from 200 to 999
  (`Response.error()` has 0, and a 1xx is no final status), reads the hook
  Response's body and, over HTTP/1.1, checks every header and Set-Cookie
  value with node's own validator, so a body that fails or a value node
  refuses answers the catch's 500 with nothing of the hook's on it; over
  HTTP/2 a status from 600 up is refused as it is set, with the same 500.
  What node's HTTP/1.1 writer refuses only as it writes the response, such
  as a `trailer` on a response it does not chunk, closes the connection,
  because `res` then holds the hook's answer. A 304 keeps the
  `content-length` the hook declares when production's `parseInt` reads it
  as a non-negative safe integer; every other length is the body's own. A
  client that goes away during the auth POST's body ended the dev server
  through an unhandled rejection; the read's error is now caught and the
  hook does not run for that request (production runs it and drops its
  answer). A declared length past 64 KiB is answered 413 before the body
  arrives, as production answers it, and a body without one is answered 413
  the moment it crosses 64 KiB, before the hook runs; the rest of the body is
  read and dropped, so an HTTP/2 stream completes.

- **`vite dev`'s auth and dashboard mounts answer only their own paths.**
  Both read the target from `req.originalUrl`, because connect strips the
  mount from `req.url` and matches it without regard to case and with a `/`
  or `.` after it: the auth lane routes the exact path only and hands the
  hook that target, dropping the `?` of an empty query as uWS does, and the
  dashboard answers its path and the paths under it, before its loopback
  gate and method check run. `dashboard.path` loses its trailing slashes, as
  `adminPath` does, and its collision check with the WebSocket and auth
  paths ignores them on either side. `test/helpers/vite-dev.js` boots a real
  Vite dev server, on `server.https` or with a cleartext HTTP/2 listener over
  its middleware stack; `test/vite-origin-parity.test.js` and
  `test/dev-dashboard.test.js` now run on it, and
  `test/vite-dev-request-shape.test.js` holds the dev auth lane to the built
  runtime by running the fixture's own hook on both.
  `test/helpers/openssl.js` takes the openssl lookup out of
  `test/tls-reload.test.js` for both suites.

- **The Host value is held to the authority grammar where a URL is built from
  it.** `get_origin` (handler/config.js) now returns `originFromHeaders`
  (utils/origin.js), which refuses a host that is not `host [":" port]` per
  RFC 3986 (`invalidHost`, utils/request-target.js), a port header that is not
  digits and a scheme that is not `http` or `https`, throwing an
  `OriginHeaderError` that names the header and never its value. The SSR lane
  answers that 400 before the body is read, where the render catch answered
  500 and logged `runtime.ssr.failed`, and answers 400 when the URL parser
  refuses what passed (a port past 65535, a malformed `xn--` label); uWS reads
  past the unread body to the next request. The admin and auth lanes already
  answered the throw 400. `get_origin` warns once when the refused header is
  a configured one, naming it and the setting that configured it
  (`refusedHeaderSetting`), and never for the Host header itself. Built
  assets, the probes and a render under `ORIGIN` build no URL from the value
  and do not read it. `bench/43-origin-host-check-cost.mjs` puts the check at
  about 17 ns per rendered request, 43 ns behind a proxy, against about 2 us
  for the Request construction alone. `test/host-header-real.test.js` and
  `test/host-header-proxy-real.test.js` pin the SSR, admin and auth lanes and
  the configured headers on the built runtime, the latter on a variant of its
  own, and the `get_origin` unit tests now drive the shipped function instead
  of a copy of it.

- **The Origin check, the test server and `vite dev` read the Host the same
  way.** `isOriginAllowed` merges `PORT_HEADER` into the host through the
  helper `originFromHeaders` uses, and a same-origin comparison refuses a Host
  that is not an authority rather than let the merge tidy it (`a:80:`) into
  one; bench/43 puts that at about 50 ns on the roughly 420 ns check an
  upgrade or auth POST makes once. The `createTestServer` admin mirror and the
  `vite dev` auth lane apply `invalidHost`, the latter before reading the body
  and with its Request construction guarded, and under `ORIGIN` the dev auth
  lane now builds its request on that origin and reads no Host, as production
  does. It also refuses an absolute-form target, which uWS answers before any
  route: connect keeps such a target's scheme and host in front of the path
  it strips, and the scheme would land in the request URL's host.

- **Exact mounts are refused on a resolved spelling.** `registerRoute` records
  every exact path it registers except a WebSocket route's, and a route that
  yields to the application takes its path back out (`yieldsToApp`, the
  WebSocket path's GET route without an admission ceiling).
  `entersExactMount` (handler/route-registry.js) asks whether a reading of the
  target, with SvelteKit's `/__data.json`, `.html__data.json` and
  `/__route.js` suffixes stripped and a data request's
  `x-sveltekit-trailing-slash` parameter applied as its router does, is one of
  them without being the raw spelling; the parameter is parsed only when a
  mount is at stake.
  The catch-all asks it of the raw, resolved and decoded path, now for every
  app rather than only beside a mounted admin route. It parses only a path
  that can drop a segment (a dot segment, `%2e`, a backslash), not every path
  with a dot or an escape, and decodes only ASCII escapes, which cannot throw,
  so an encoded prefix spelling ending in a bad escape is judged too.
  `bench/42-resolution-gate-cost.mjs` finds the gate adding, without an admin
  route, 10-28 ns to a plain or dotted path, about 60 ns to a data request,
  about 78 ns to an escaped non-ASCII path and about 365 ns to a dot segment;
  with the admin route mounted a data request drops from 331 to 65 ns and an
  escaped path from 584 to 92 ns. `test/route-registry.test.js` pins the
  predicate, `test/request-target-real.test.js` dot segments, an encoded dot
  segment, an encoded letter and the data and route suffixes onto the probes,
  an app page and its data still served, the page one trailing slash further
  on and its data left to the app, and the WebSocket path left to the app
  without a ceiling; `test/admin-prefix-entry-real.test.js` pins resolved
  and encoded prefix spellings ending in an undecodable escape, and a raw byte
  or a fragment on the admin lane.

- **An encoded spelling of a static file's name finds it.** After the
  prerendered lookup misses, a GET or HEAD whose target carries a `%` looks
  it up decoded with `decodeURI`, as sirv decodes before its file lookup
  (`encodedStaticEntry`, handler/static-assets.js), and serves a hit through
  `serveStatic` under an `adapter.http.static` span. `cacheDir` also keys a
  name's NFC form, as sirv does, where it differs, is still not ASCII, and no
  file holds that key; a file's own name replaces such an alias.
  `test/request-target-real.test.js` serves `test/fixture/static/maß.txt` for
  `/ma%C3%9F.txt` and its lowercase escapes, refuses its raw bytes, does not
  serve `/.well-known%2Fprobe.txt` as the file behind the separator, and,
  through the built index, finds a name with a space and a name written
  decomposed, keeps an alias from shadowing a file in either walk order, and
  registers no alias that composes to ASCII.

- **The upgrade carry rides private Symbols.** The request id and trace
  context cross `res.upgrade()` on `CARRY_REQUEST_ID` and
  `CARRY_TRACE_CONTEXT` (utils/request-id.js), and the admission permit on a
  Symbol each `createConnectionPermitCarrier()` makes; all three rode string
  keys an accessor on `Object.prototype` could intercept. uWS copies every
  enumerable own property of the upgrade userData, Symbol keys included, by
  assignment, and the testing typings now say so. The permit carrier no
  longer needs its collision fallback keys. `open` records a
  `ws.request-id-carry` assertion and mints an id if one ever fails to
  arrive, on every surface.
  `test/upgrade-carry-real.test.js` boots the built server with accessors
  installed for every old key and requires the connection to open with its
  request id; `test/connection-permit-carrier.test.js` pins the carrier
  against an assignment copy.

- **A read in progress ends when the client goes.** `readBody` hands the abort
  a way to error its stream (`state.failBody`), and both lanes' `onAborted`
  call it, so a read waiting on a chunk the client will never send rejects
  instead of pending forever. `test/request-signal-real.test.js` pins it
  through a partial body whose request is released.

- **Tracked membership joins the shared cohort of the connection's own server.**
  `trackedSubscribe` and `trackedUnsubscribe` read the cohort join and leave
  from `Symbol.for` slots each surface sets on its base platform, where they
  used to call a process-wide hook the production handler installed at
  import. `createTestServer` sets its own, and the close path empties the
  connection's cohort set once it has released it, so a late leave in the
  simulator cannot release a reference twice. `test/shared-fanout.test.js`
  pins the join, a second join, the leave, two servers in one process and the
  simulator's late leave; `test/subscriptions-entry-real.test.js` pins the
  production join and leave through the public entry.

- **Every envelope builder refuses data JSON has no form for.**
  `envelopeData` (utils/epoch.js) is the `JSON.stringify` the builders already
  made plus a check that it returned a string; `completeEnvelope`,
  `completeGameEnvelope`, the production send lanes and the `vite dev`
  builders call it. Benchmarked before/after on `completeEnvelope` across three
  shapes: within run noise. `test/envelope-data.test.js` pins the helper, both
  builders and a `createTestServer` publish.

- **Extra `__` entries are imported by the file Rollup wrote.**
  `writeAndCloseRollupBundle` returns the write result, and the new
  `extraEntryImports` maps each entry to its output chunk by its source module,
  so a name Rollup sanitised still resolves; specifiers are JSON-quoted. The
  directory listing is sorted, so entries load in the same order on NTFS and
  ext4, and `docs/architecture.md` states the entry contract.
  `test/extra-entry-imports.test.js` runs a real Rollup build of `__a#b`,
  `__it's` and `__plain` and imports the generated index.

- **`CloseContext.bytesOut` documents its unit.** Binary frames count bytes and
  text frames count UTF-16 code units, the unit `topicPublishBytesPerSec`
  already documents. Exact UTF-8 was measured with `Buffer.byteLength` against
  `length` on real envelope shapes (+28 ns at 90 characters, +140 ns at 400,
  per send) and declined for a stat every send updates.

- **Each connection attempt is bounded.** `openSocket` arms a 15-second timer
  that closes a socket still `CONNECTING`, so its close event takes the
  existing reconnect path, and the auth preflight's `fetch` carries an
  `AbortSignal` on the same bound, so an abandoned preflight is a transient
  failure like a network error. Both timers are cleared when the attempt
  settles. `test/client-real.test.js` holds a handshake and a preflight open
  under fake timers and requires the retry after the bound, and fails with the
  bound removed.

- **A 429 from the auth preflight is throttling, not refusal.** The client's
  preflight classified `status >= 400 && < 500` as unauthorized and set the
  permanently-closed flag. A 429 now takes its own `throttled` outcome: the
  failure store reads `class: 'THROTTLE'`, the backoff jumps ahead as for a
  4429 close, and `scheduleReconnect` takes the parsed `Retry-After` (seconds
  or an HTTP date, capped at five minutes) as a floor under the backoff delay.
  The production preflight's 429 now writes that header. `test/client-real.test.js`
  pins the client with fake timers, and `test/auth-throttle-real.test.js` drives
  the built runtime past the budget and reads the header.

- **The control-egress figures name the shape that amplifies most.** Measured
  on the built runtime: 1,344 shortest-legal topics in 8,121 bytes draw 1,344
  frames and 97,484 bytes; the 256-topic cap padded with empty strings, which
  past the cap are only type-checked and each answered with a denial, draws
  2,466 frames and 174,956 bytes for 8,175. README, `control-egress.js`,
  `byte-budget.js` and the suite's header now quote the second.

- **`sendWireBatch` returns the status of its last send in every branch.** The
  JSON fallback started its result at 1, so when the dropped binary frame was
  the final entry there was nothing left to send and the 1 was returned. The
  fallback now takes the status it continues from. `test/send-wire-batch-shed.test.js`
  drives both surfaces with a scripted socket and fails on each without it.

- **Every production platform member is declared on `Platform`.**
  `platform.assertions` was the one missing. `test/platform-type-surface.test.js`
  now reads the platform object literal with a parser and requires each of its
  members on the interface, so the next undeclared one fails a test.

- **A cut diagnostic message is trimmed again after the cut.**
  `normalizeDiagnosticMessage` (diagnostic-format.js) collapsed whitespace and
  trimmed before cutting to 512 characters, so the cut could end on a space;
  the parser compares the message with its normalized form and with the
  physical line, and refused both. `test/diagnostic-format.test.js` places a
  space at every position from 505 to 515 and requires each formatted line to
  parse as canonical, and fails at 511 without the second trim.

- **A failing `open`, `drain` or `close` hook costs one connection, not the
  worker.** The hosts call these hooks from a transport callback and never
  await them. A synchronous throw out of a uWS callback is an
  uncaughtException - the runtime's handler exits the worker, and in
  single-process mode Node exits the process - and a rejection is an
  unhandled rejection. `runOpenHook`, `runDrainHook` and `runCloseHook`
  (utils/hook-boundary.js) catch both wherever the surface calls the hook:
  open and drain close their connection with 1011, while close only logs,
  because its connection is already gone and the host's teardown after it
  must still run. The `then` read sits inside the same try as the call, so a
  returned value whose `then` getter throws is contained too. Under
  `vite dev` a throwing close hook also skipped removing the connection from
  the dev server's live maps. `test/error-registry-hook-crash.test.js` drives
  each lane against the built runtime and requires a bystander and a new
  connection to be served afterwards; `test/lifecycle-hook-boundary.test.js`
  drives open and close on `createTestServer` and `vite dev` and requires the
  next connection to be served. Both fail with the boundary removed.

- **An unserializable `sendCoalesced` value is contained at the flush.**
  Serialization is deferred to the flush on purpose, so a key overwritten a
  thousand times pays one `JSON.stringify`. A value queued behind
  backpressure was therefore first serialized from the uWS drain callback,
  and a throw there is an uncaughtException. `flushCoalescedFor`
  (handler/subscribe-hooks.js) now catches the serializer, and also refuses
  a result that is not a string (a function or a symbol), drops that entry
  and keeps draining. When the failing entry is the one the calling
  `sendCoalesced` just set, the flush is inside that call and the error is
  rethrown to it; otherwise it is reported as
  `ADAPTER-ERR-COALESCED-UNSERIALIZABLE`. `test/coalesced-drain-real.test.js`
  backs a real socket up past `maxBackpressure` with a client that stops
  reading, queues a good and a BigInt value, and requires the good one
  delivered, the bad one reported and the connection still serving, on the
  built runtime and on `createTestServer`; with the containment removed the
  built runtime's case fails with the escaped throw.

- **`createTestServer` queues coalesced sends and drains them.** Its platform
  had no `sendCoalesced` and its socket behaviour no `drain`, so a suite using
  either met a missing method or a hook that never ran. It now keeps the same
  per-connection pending map as production, flushes it through the outbound
  chokepoint (so chaos scenarios apply), and on each drain flushes and then
  runs the app hook inside the lifecycle boundary.

- **The README's retry-stopping example sends the code it names.** It called
  `ws.close(4401, 'Unauthorized')`; uWS's `close()` ignores arguments and
  sends no close frame, so the bundled client read 1006, classed it as
  retryable and reconnected. The example uses `ws.end()`, and the README's
  list of socket methods now says what each of the two sends.

## [0.6.0-next.95] - 2026-09-22

<!-- consumer-release-summary:start -->
### Consumer summary

- **Added: an app-driven topic epoch mint.** Changing a topic's seq authority - counter to external allocator, partition to partition, a reset store - left client offsets pointing into a seq space that no longer continues them, with nothing repudiating them; `bumpTopicEpoch(topic)` now mints that topic a fresh generation so those offsets cold-rehydrate at their next resume.
  - **Affects:** Apps whose topics change seq authority at runtime; every other topic keeps the process generation exactly as before.
  - **Action:** None unless you change an authority - then call it on each worker where the change lands, since app code runs on every worker and the equality-only epoch repudiates old offsets everywhere identically.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** The subscribe ack and resume compares pick the minted value up through the same read authority `topicEpoch` wraps; the override rides the bounded per-topic map the relay-loss mint already uses. `createTestServer` and `vite dev` now answer per-topic epochs through the same shared module.
  - **Detail:** [Added engineering detail](#added).
- **Added: the send lanes take an explicit gap-fill `seq`.** A resume hook replaying history had no way to put per-frame sequence numbers on what it sent; `options.seq` on `send` and `sendWire` now stamps the envelope and the binary frame's seq slot identically, side-effect-free - no counter advances, nothing recorded or captured.
  - **Affects:** Resume hooks and replay backends doing gap-fill through the send lanes; every existing call is byte-identical without the option.
  - **Action:** None to keep current behavior. Gap-fill replay passes each frame's stored seq: `platform.send(ws, topic, event, data, { seq })`.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** Number and bigint take the publish lanes' validation and safe-integer range; `false`/`null`/absent mean no seq; `true` throws, since the send lanes have no counter to draw. `sendWireBatch` deliberately takes no seq option - one value cannot be one-seq-per-entry; replay discrete frames through `sendWire`.
  - **Detail:** [Added engineering detail](#added).
- **Added: the static lane answers the full RFC 9110 precondition set.** Mutable assets now serve `Last-Modified` beside the `ETag` and honor `If-Match` and `If-Unmodified-Since` with 412, `If-Modified-Since` with 304, and the list and `*` forms of both entity headers, evaluated in the RFC's order so a failed `If-Match` is never converted into a 304.
  - **Affects:** Caches and clients revalidating static and prerendered responses; a cache that lost the ETag can now revalidate by date instead of re-downloading every full body.
  - **Action:** None. Versioned immutable assets are unchanged - their filename is the validator and they carry neither header.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** Every request that answered 304 before still does; the new answers only add 304s and 412s where the RFC requires them. `If-Match` compares by opaque equality against any validator the lane issued, because every validator is weak by construction and strict strong comparison would refuse the exact tag the server handed out. `last-modified` joins the reserved `staticHeaders` keys, since the date preconditions answer from the file's real time.
  - **Detail:** [Added engineering detail](#added).
- **Added: a displaced subscription-accounting sink now says so.** The counter lives in one `globalThis` slot, so a second copy of the runtime in one worker silently takes every delta - freezing one total while the other is charged releases it never matched; installing over a different sink is now `ADAPTER-ERR-SUBSCRIPTION-SINK-DISPLACED`.
  - **Affects:** Deployments or suites where two copies of the adapter runtime load in one worker - a duplicated dependency instance, or two built fixtures imported by one test process. A single copy never reaches it.
  - **Action:** None unless it fires; then deduplicate the runtime instance rather than the counter, which is a symptom.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** Clearing the slot to `null` and reinstalling the same function are not displacements, so releasing the slot stays ordinary. This names the topology; it does not change how subscriptions are counted.
  - **Detail:** [Added engineering detail](#added).
- **Added: the cluster simulator can fail a worker's relay attach.** `attachFailWorker(id)` on the multi-worker scenario API models a worker that reports ready and never reports its relay reader live, and `metrics.attachFailures` counts it; the simulator now judges workers through the primary's own sweep and slot fields, so the attach regime is reachable from a scenario.
  - **Affects:** Anyone running `svelte-adapter-uws/sim` multi-worker scenarios; the production primary's behaviour is unchanged.
  - **Action:** None. Existing scenarios and seeds reproduce as before; the new fault is opt-in per scenario.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** Additive. The simulator's restart budget now resets on the attach rather than on ready, the edge the primary stamps it on; no existing scenario goes ready without attaching, so no recorded run changes. The fault models the detection only: the simulated bus still delivers relay frames to a worker in that state.
  - **Detail:** [Added engineering detail](#added).
- **Added: the control/ack channel is bounded per connection.** It amplifies - a client names a topic in a few bytes and is answered with a whole frame - so a connection may now be sent 4 MiB of protocol frames per 10-second window, and one that exceeds it is closed with 4429 rather than served.
  - **Affects:** Every deployment. Measured at the worst legal shape, one 8 KB `subscribe-batch` is answered with about 97 KB across 1,345 frames, and nothing rate-limited the repetition: every `messageAdmission` ceiling is disabled unless configured.
  - **Action:** None. A reconnecting client restoring 256 topics spends about 15 KB of the window and a 5,000-topic restore about 300 KB, so a healthy burst is orders of magnitude clear of it.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option. The ceiling is fixed rather than configurable.
  - **Compatibility:** Only frames the adapter emits in answer to a client are charged - acks, denials on both the JSON and the binary game lane, `wire-id` announces, protocol errors, `welcome`, `lease-ok`, window grants - measured in UTF-8 bytes on the wire. Application `send` and `publish` are never charged here and the tenant egress budgets are unchanged. The close is 4429, which the bundled client already classes as throttling and reconnects on; nothing new goes on the wire, because the protocol is frozen at revision 1, and the operator is told through `ADAPTER-ERR-CONTROL-EGRESS-EXHAUSTED`, carrying the connection's request id, instead. A `registerIngress` route now receives the surface's budgeted sender as its sixth argument, so a consumer route can charge a denial of its own; a route written against the five-argument shape keeps working.
  - **Detail:** [Added engineering detail](#added).
- **Changed: a subscription-drift report now says how many connections it summed and how many a close had already settled.** A membership counted twice and a closed connection still in the live set produce the same sum, so the two quantities that separate them now ride on the report instead of being reconstructed by whoever reads it.
  - **Affects:** Anyone reading `subs.total-mismatch` diagnostics; the two existing fields are unchanged and two more are added beside them.
  - **Action:** None. A reader keying on `totalSubscriptions` and `summed` keeps working.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** Additive. `connections` is always present on a mismatch; `settled` appears only when the snapshot could answer, so an absent field means unmeasured rather than zero.
  - **Detail:** [Changed engineering detail](#changed).
- **Changed: the `seq` publish option speaks one table, and refuses what it cannot carry.** A value outside the contract - a numeric string, an object - now throws naming the legal forms instead of silently drawing the local counter, and an integer past the wire's safe-integer range throws instead of rounding; `{ seq: null }` means no seq, and `bigint` joins `number`.
  - **Affects:** Callers passing seq values outside `boolean | number` - a numeric string from a JSON column was the typical accident - and, separately, callers passing an integer above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, such as a snowflake or a large Kafka offset, which previously published as a rounded value. Also `publishWireBatch` entries, where `true`, `false`, and `null` now act per entry as overrides of the shared options instead of falling through silently.
  - **Action:** Pass a number or bigint for an explicit authority's value, `false` or `null` for no seq, `true` or nothing for the counter. A caller that relied on a non-contract value drawing the counter should say `true`. An authority whose ids run above the safe-integer range needs the wide id moved into the event data, or offset by a per-topic base, since `seq` now refuses it rather than rounding it.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** Absent, `true`, `false`, and in-range numbers behave exactly as before, on every lane and every surface (production, `createTestServer`, `vite dev`). `null` moves from counter to no-seq; non-contract values move from counter to `TypeError`. Two breaks to know about: an integer above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` moves from a silently rounded publish to a `TypeError`, because the double seq space stops having a neighbour at distance one there and adjacent ids collapse onto one value, which stalls a client watermark that only advances on a strict greater-than.
  - **Detail:** [Changed engineering detail](#changed).
- **Changed: four metric help strings describe what is counted rather than which layer counted it.** `# HELP` named a native C++ fan-out and a native backpressure limit; those are implementation details, and a help string an operator reads to interpret a number should not require knowing which runtime produced it.
  - **Affects:** Anyone reading `# HELP` on the metrics endpoint for `ws_publishes_total`, `ws_publish_outcomes_total`, `ws_dropped_frames_total` or `ws_dropped_bytes_total`. No metric name, type, label or value changes.
  - **Action:** None. A dashboard or alert keying on names and labels is unaffected; only the description text differs.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** Text only, and the meanings are unchanged - "never per-recipient deliveries" and "dropped under backpressure" say the same thing without naming the runtime. The declaration in `src/index.d.ts` keeps this adapter's specifics, and now states one an operator would otherwise meet on a dashboard: a publish that excludes a socket is delivered by a per-socket walk rather than one native call, so it is counted by `ws_publishes_total` and absent from the outcome breakdown - the two do not sum.
  - **Detail:** [Changed engineering detail](#changed).

- **Changed: one connection may hold 65,536 subscriptions, down from 1,000,000.** A landed subscription is a native topic-tree entry, measured at about 700 bytes resident each, so one admitted connection could hold about 700 MB that the connection ceiling cannot see; the 65,537th subscribe is denied with `RATE_LIMITED` and everything held stays.
  - **Affects:** Only a client subscribed to more than 65,536 distinct topics at once on one connection; the pending-attempt cap, the request cap and every other retained-state cap are unchanged.
  - **Action:** None for any client under the cap. A client that legitimately needs more topics than that on one connection should fan out per entity group rather than per entity, which the wire lanes are built for.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option; the cap is not exposed.
  - **Compatibility:** The denial is the same `subscribe-denied` with reason `RATE_LIMITED` the old cap answered, on the production runtime, `createTestServer` and `vite dev` alike; nothing already subscribed is touched.
  - **Detail:** [Changed engineering detail](#changed).
- **Fixed: a `staticHeaders` value carrying a newline is refused at build time.** A CR, LF or NUL in a configured value reached `res.writeHeader` verbatim, where it ends the header field and starts whatever follows - header injection, or a second response; names are now held to the RFC 9110 token grammar too.
  - **Affects:** Builds configuring `staticHeaders`. A value or name that could split a response now fails the build instead of shipping.
  - **Action:** None for a valid configuration. A build that starts failing was emitting a header a client could not have read correctly - remove the control character from the value, or correct a name that is not a bare HTTP token.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** Refused at build rather than sanitised at request time, so an operator is told rather than quietly served something other than what they configured. Every name the token grammar allows still passes, including the punctuation set, and names are lowercased as before.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: a respawning worker is no longer quarantined for the relay backlog its boot could not drain.** A crashed worker's replacement filled its ring while booting and the age ceiling read that as a stall, respawning it until the restart limit killed the process; the primary now skips a worker in the fan-out until it reports its reader live.
  - **Affects:** Multi-worker deployments with the relay ring enabled, under enough relay traffic to fill a booting worker's ring inside its boot time.
  - **Action:** None.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** Both ceilings and the `bytes`/`age` quarantine reasons are unchanged; what changed is that a booting worker is no longer handed frames to be judged on. A worker publishing into the relay before its siblings have attached reaches fewer of them, which the receiving worker already treated as a stream joined mid-flight rather than a lost frame.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: a recover subscribe without a `ref` is refused loudly instead of dying silently.** A subscribe asking for history could hit the saturated gate and get nothing back, leaving the client believing itself subscribed and resuming into a silent gap; it now gets `{"type":"error","code":"RECOVER_REQUIRES_REF"}` up front, on all three server surfaces.
  - **Affects:** Hand-rolled clients only; the bundled client stamps a `ref` on every path, including the reconnect resubscribe batch.
  - **Action:** Include a `ref` on any subscribe that carries `recover`. A `subscribe-batch` naming history in its recover map needs its one `ref` for the same reason.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** Plain ref-less subscribes keep their documented silence, and `recover` against a server with no resume hook stays ignored - there is no history to miss. The refusal engages only where the recover lane would.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: the cursor plugin stops decoding and parsing frames the runtime already parsed.** Its message hook now reads the pre-parsed envelope the adapter hands every hook, which also removes a per-message decoder allocation and a crash on a frame whose whole body is null.
  - **Affects:** Every connection on a server with the cursor plugin installed, since that hook inspects each frame before the application's own handler sees it.
  - **Action:** None.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** No wire or API change. Binary frames, frames over 8 KiB and anything the adapter did not pre-parse still take the decode path, which now shares one process-wide decoder.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: the consistency auditor no longer reports a subscription drift that never happened.** A connection whose native handle was freed while the auditor walked it was skipped from the window but still counted by the cap accountant, so the cross-check compared a complete counter against a short sum and reported a mismatch no membership explained.
  - **Affects:** Deployments running the per-worker consistency auditor (`CONSISTENCY_AUDIT_INTERVAL_MS`) on a worker small enough for its whole population to fit one audit window; the rate tracked connection churn, so a busy worker reported more of them.
  - **Action:** None. Re-read any `subs.total-mismatch` history against this fix before treating it as evidence.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** No wire, option, or metric name moved. A window that omits any connection now withholds the cap accountant instead of cross-checking against a partial sum, which is what a partial slice already did; a complete window still runs every check.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: a batch call's `excludeWs` now excludes on both lanes.** `publishWireBatch` honoured a call-level exclusion only for stateless codecs, so opting a codec into batch framing silently dropped it and the author heard its own updates back; the call-level socket now defaults every entry, and a per-entry `excludeWs` overrides it, on either lane.
  - **Affects:** Callers passing `excludeWs` on `publishWireBatch`'s options with a stateful codec - previously ignored there without an error.
  - **Action:** None. Per-entry exclusions behave exactly as before.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** The batch-level form is now documented on both surfaces; it was honoured undocumented on the stateless lane and ignored on the stateful one. An entry-level `null` exclusion now means absent (inherit the call-level default) on both lanes, where the stateless lane previously read it as an override to nothing.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: the cluster relay's frame ceiling now measures encoded bytes.** It compared UTF-16 string length, so a multibyte-heavy frame up to three times the configured size passed the sender and could land over every sibling worker's byte-measured backlog ceiling at once - the mass quarantine the ceiling exists to prevent.
  - **Affects:** Multi-worker deployments that set `CLUSTER_RELAY_MAX_FRAME_KB` and relay non-ASCII payloads; ASCII payloads measured identically before and after.
  - **Action:** None. A deployment relying on the old undercount to sneak larger multibyte frames through should raise the ceiling to the size it actually intends.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** Strictly tighter: encoded bytes are never fewer than code units, so nothing previously refused is now admitted. Refusal reports carry the exact encoded size.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: a `seq` the wire cannot carry is refused even while an egress ceiling is shedding.** The publish lanes validated the value as a side effect of stamping, which happens after the ceiling decides, so a bad `seq` came back as an ordinary-looking `false` under load and threw only once traffic dropped.
  - **Affects:** Callers passing a `seq` outside the contract while an egress budget is armed. With no budget configured the refusal already arrived immediately and nothing changes.
  - **Action:** None. The `TypeError` that now arrives on the offending call was always the correct answer; it was previously deferred to the first quiet window, pointing at a deploy that could be weeks old.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** The refusals, their messages and their classes are unchanged - only their timing is. A refused value charges no egress and advances no counter. `publishWireBatch` now takes the same decision at its call gate, so an empty batch refuses what a full one refuses, on production, `createTestServer` and `vite dev` alike.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: a batch that refuses one message's `seq` no longer publishes the ones before it.** The atomic pre-pass asked only whether the deployment was clustered, and that question answers accepted without reading the value on a single worker - so `batch()` delivered a prefix and `publishBatched()` spent sequence numbers on frames it never sent.
  - **Affects:** Single-worker deployments - the default - calling `batch()` or `publishBatched()` with a `seq` outside the contract on any message but the first. Multi-worker runtimes already refused these at the pre-pass.
  - **Action:** None. The same `TypeError` is thrown; what changes is that it arrives before anything has been published or stamped.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** No accepted call behaves differently. A refused `publishBatched` no longer advances the per-topic counter, so a topic's sequence no longer skips values that never reached a client - which is what made this hard to see, since nothing on the wire marks such a gap. `createTestServer` takes the same order on both surfaces.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: the admin route refuses a target that normalizes out of its own prefix.** The route matched the raw request target while the `Request` handed to `admin()` had its dot segments resolved, so `GET /__realtime/../reflect` reached the handler describing itself as `/reflect` - a path outside the namespace that handler dispatches and authorizes on.
  - **Affects:** Apps exporting an `admin(request)` handler, on the auto-mounted route. Every ordinary target is unaffected, including one that resolves back inside the prefix.
  - **Action:** None. An admin handler that assumed `request.url` lay inside its prefix was right to; it now always does.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** Such a target now answers 400 before any body is read, instead of reaching the handler. A percent-encoded `..%2f` is a single opaque segment rather than a dot segment, so it keeps the prefix and is still served. `createTestServer` takes the same decision.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: `protection: 'auto'` was documented as inert without an admission ceiling, and is not.** Escalation to `'elevated'` reads the pressure sampler alone, and that sampler runs unconditionally - so an app setting only `protection: 'auto'` does reach elevated, where every refusal widens its `Retry-After` jitter.
  - **Affects:** Anyone who read the declaration and concluded `'auto'` did nothing without `upgradeAdmission`. No behaviour changed; the description did.
  - **Action:** None, unless the wording drove a configuration choice - `'auto'` without a ceiling is a working configuration that stops at elevated.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** Documentation only. What genuinely needs a ceiling is the auto step INTO `'siege'`, which compares over-capacity rejects against that ceiling's admit rate; a pinned `'elevated'` or `'siege'` needs no ceiling either.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: a worker's uncaught exception costs one worker, not the process.** A worker thread holds uWS socket handles Node does not track, so tearing the thread down after an uncaught exception closed the libuv loop with a poll handle still active and aborted the process - the supervisor never got to replace anything.
  - **Affects:** Clustered deployments (`workers`), where an uncaught exception in a worker could end the whole process instead of one thread. Single-process deployments are unaffected.
  - **Action:** None.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** The `cluster.worker-error` event still fires with the same shape, so dashboards and alerts are unchanged; the worker now exits cleanly and is replaced. An application that installs its own `uncaughtException` handler keeps today's behaviour exactly - Node leaves such a worker alive, and the runtime defers whenever it is not the only listener.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: the posture export describes the whole deployment under `workers`.** One socket path cannot have several owners, so every worker unlinked the previous one's socket and bound its own: a consumer read one bind-order-chosen thread's posture and believed it was the server's, and any worker's shutdown removed the live socket.
  - **Affects:** Deployments setting both `postureExport` and `workers`. Single-process deployments are untouched.
  - **Action:** None. The documented path is the same path.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** The primary owns the socket and serves the highest posture any worker is in, carrying that worker's own reason and pressure numbers. The line gains an additive `workers` count of the threads it summarizes; single-process lines do not carry it. The 1 Hz cadence is unchanged; under `workers` its liveness meaning is the PRIMARY's, and a worker that stops reporting keeps its last posture on the line until the heartbeat watchdog terminates it and its exit drops it, about 30 seconds.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: `publishWire` no longer treats an application's options as a relayed frame.** The cross-worker relay marked its re-entry with two ordinary option keys, so an app that set them was handled as a sibling worker's relay: it named the topic's seq itself, uncounted, past an armed egress ceiling, and out over the relay.
  - **Affects:** Apps calling `platform.publishWire` directly, including through a plugin codec. No documented option changes and no ordinary call behaves differently.
  - **Action:** None.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** Those two keys are now inert - a call carrying them publishes as any other origin publish would, drawing the topic counter. In a multi-worker runtime such a call meets the same sequence-authority refusal every other publish meets, which is a `TypeError` where it previously published silently. The batch-admission marker is hardened the same way: an options object that answers for every key no longer gets a publish past a crossed egress ceiling. `createTestServer` and the dev plugin take the same decisions.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: the reserved admin prefix now holds against a target that arrives inside it.** The mount matches the raw target while the lanes behind it resolve and percent-decode, so `/foo/../__realtime/introspect` and `/%5f%5frealtime/introspect` both skipped the admin lane and reached the app's own routing inside the reserved namespace.
  - **Affects:** Apps exporting an `admin(request)` handler, where the mount is what reserves the prefix. Without one there is no mount, no reservation, and nothing changes.
  - **Action:** None. An app that read `/__realtime/*` as a prefix its own routes never see was right to; that now holds for the resolved and the encoded spellings alike.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** Such a target now answers 400 instead of reaching the app, which is the same answer the opposite direction already gives. A dot segment or an escape that lands somewhere ordinary is unaffected - the check is about where a path ends up, so those still resolve and are served normally. The bare prefix stays on the catch-all, exactly as when it is spelled directly. Worth knowing where the reservation is part of a security boundary: a fronting proxy's ACL on the literal prefix sees none of these spellings, so the adapter is what refuses them.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: a socket leaves the live set before the rest of its close teardown.** The close released the permit, the subscription accounting, the capability counts and the wire states before removing the connection, and none of those is individually guarded - so one throw stranded a socket whose handle was gone in every publish walk and in the auditor's sum, permanently.
  - **Affects:** Every deployment, on the connection close path. Nothing about a close that completes changes.
  - **Action:** None.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** The removal owes nothing to the releases that followed it, so moving it first changes only what survives a throw among them. A stranded entry read as a ledger mismatch no double charge explained and never cleared, which is the shape that no longer occurs.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: a relay frame length with its top bit set no longer wedges the reader.** The ring decoded the four-byte prefix with `|`, which yields a signed result, so such a prefix read negative - under the oversized ceiling, under the bytes on hand, and into a parse offset that emitted empty frames until it climbed back to zero.
  - **Affects:** Multi-worker deployments with the cluster relay enabled, on a corrupt or hostile length prefix - the input class the ceiling exists for.
  - **Action:** None.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** Read unsigned, those same bytes are an enormous frame, which is what they claim to be and what the ceiling already refuses. Every length the ring accepted before is unchanged.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: `If-Range` is evaluated with the strong comparison RFC 9110 requires.** Every validator this lane issues is weak by construction, and the range gate took one as a match - so a client could splice a slice onto bytes from a representation that merely shared a validator, and read a corrupt body under a 206 saying it was fine.
  - **Affects:** Clients sending `If-Range` with an entity tag against a static or prerendered asset. A plain `Range` is untouched, which is what a resuming download manager sends.
  - **Action:** None. A client wanting the range without the consistency claim sends `Range` alone.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** A weak `If-Range` now falls through to the full 200 representation - the fallback a malformed or multi-range header already takes - where it previously answered 206. Since every validator this lane issues is weak, that is every entity-tag `If-Range` it sees; a date `If-Range` is unchanged.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: a resume frame's epoch map takes the same grant gate as its sequence numbers.** `lastSeenSeqs` had its ungranted topics dropped and `lastSeenEpochs` reached the hook exactly as parsed, so the gate dropped a client-named topic from one hand and returned it with the other - carrying its generation as well as its name.
  - **Affects:** Deployments with a resume hook and the wire-subscribe grant gate armed. Both maps arrive on one frame and the hook reads them together, so an ungranted topic was visible through the epoch half.
  - **Action:** None.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** Both maps now take one filter, written once so they cannot drift. A granted topic's epoch reaches the hook exactly as before.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: an ephemeral port under reuseport is refused instead of booting a fleet nothing routes to.** Every reuseport worker calls `listen()` for itself, so `PORT=0` hands each of them a different port and the single shared port the mode exists to provide never happens - while the balancer, the health check and the startup log all name port 0.
  - **Affects:** Linux deployments setting `PORT=0` with reuseport cluster mode. Acceptor mode is untouched and must be: the primary binds once and hands descriptors down, so one ephemeral port is still one port.
  - **Action:** Name a real port. Off Linux nothing changes - reuseport is already refused there by its own id, which fires first.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** Refused as `ADAPTER-ERR-CLUSTER-CONFIG-PORT` with the other capacity misconfigurations, before any worker spawns, so the failure is at boot rather than in the routing layer.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: a certificate watch that dies after starting no longer takes the process down.** Nothing listened for the watcher's `error` event, and an unhandled one is rethrown, so a watch the platform reported as failed after start raised an uncaught exception on a healthy serving process, and on a cluster primary that ends the whole fleet.
  - **Affects:** TLS deployments with the certificate watch on, which is the default. A watch that fails to START was always caught; this is the one that fails later, which arrives as an event rather than a throw.
  - **Action:** None. If the new line appears, find what stopped the watch - a permission change on the certificate directory, or the platform's watch resources running out - and restart.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** The process now stays up and reports `ADAPTER-ERR-TLS-WATCH-LOST`, or `ADAPTER-ERR-TLS-PRIMARY-WATCH-LOST` on a cluster primary, and enters the same degraded TLS state a watch that never started produces - sticky, so no later success clears it. Its own id rather than the existing watch ids, because the operator's next move differs.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: removing or replacing the certificate directory no longer spins or silently kills the watcher.** No platform reports that as an error - Windows narrates the deletion at about a hundred thousand events a second, Linux says one word and goes quiet - so the watcher now checks the directory's identity whenever an event names the directory itself, and ends the watch.
  - **Affects:** TLS deployments with the certificate watch on. On Windows a removed directory was a permanent CPU burn, a log line every debounce window and, on a cluster primary, a reload broadcast to every worker on the same cadence; on Linux it was a watch that looked healthy and would never see another renewal.
  - **Action:** None. If the line appears, restart the process once the directory is back where the configuration points.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** The watch ends with `ADAPTER-ERR-TLS-WATCH-LOST` (or the primary id) and the same sticky degraded state as any other dead watch; a directory replaced by a new one at the same path is read once more first, so a certificate that arrived with the replacement is served, and on the primary that reload is broadcast. Windows delivers no event for a directory moved aside, so that case stays as before: silent until restart.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: the request-dedup leader decides sharing before it holds the body.** It read the whole response and only then compared it with the 512 KB cap, so every anonymous GET of a big file sat in memory in full; a declared length past the cap now streams at once and an undeclared body is read only up to the cap.
  - **Affects:** Deployments serving large bodies (media, downloads, generated exports) from a route to clients without a `Cookie` or `Authorization` header. Measured on the field report's shape, two anonymous viewers of a 128 MB file exceeded a 1 GiB container.
  - **Action:** None. Bodies within the cap are shared exactly as before.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** A body past the cap is never shared, so concurrent anonymous requests for it each render, as they already did; what changes is that the leader streams it from the first chunk instead of after the last. A body that passes the cap mid-read streams on from where the read stopped, without re-rendering or losing a byte. A multi-chunk compressible body past the cap used to be collapsed into one chunk by the buffering and compressed; it now streams uncompressed, as the credentialed path already did, while a single-chunk body is compressed as before.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: a streamed body reaches the client whole; the older addon pin cut it.** The 0.5 line's native build (`uWebSockets.js` v20.67.0) loses the writable wakeup at the first backpressure event, which any body past the socket buffer produces at any client speed; this line pins v20.69.0, which carries the upstream fix.
  - **Affects:** On the 0.5.x line, any streamed response larger than the socket's send buffer, a few hundred kilobytes on a real link at any client speed, gigabit included: every returning visitor or authenticated user downloading media or exports (a cookie skips the buffering dedup path and takes the streaming write). Reproduced on Linux with v20.67.0 at 180 to 260 KB of a 1 MiB body; the same loop completes under v20.69.0.
  - **Action:** On 0.6.0-next, none. On 0.5.x, install `uWebSockets.js` v20.69.0 or newer alongside the adapter until a 0.5.x patch moves the pin.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option on this line.
  - **Compatibility:** No adapter code on the write path changes; the writer's drain contract is unchanged and proven under backpressure on the pinned build.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: a custom 101 header named `Connection`, `Upgrade` or `Sec-WebSocket-Accept` is refused instead of written beside the server's own.** The upgrade-header check refused unsafe bytes and non-token names but not the names the handshake writes itself, so an application value went out as a second line and a conforming client refused the handshake silently.
  - **Affects:** Applications returning `upgradeResponse()` headers named `Connection`, `Upgrade`, `Sec-WebSocket-Accept`, `Sec-WebSocket-Extensions` or `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`, in any letter case, on the production runtime, `createTestServer` or `vite dev`.
  - **Action:** Remove the header; the server writes the first three on every handshake and negotiates the last two from the client's offer. A subprotocol is selected by the client's offer, not by a response header set from the hook.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** Refused the way an unsafe byte is: `upgradeResponse()` throws a `TypeError` naming the header, and a duck-typed result carrying one takes the hook-error path (500, no 101, nothing written). Every other header name is unchanged. Values in the 0x80-0xFF range stay legal and leave as UTF-8 on every surface, which the suites now pin as the one spelling.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: the test server's admin lane answers `TRACE`, `TRACK` and `CONNECT` with 405 and an `Allow` header.** The production edge has refused the three fetch-forbidden methods since next.91; the `createTestServer` admin lane still let them throw out of `Request` construction and answered 400, so a test written against it could not see the production answer.
  - **Affects:** Test suites that drive the admin lane of `svelte-adapter-uws/testing` with those methods; the production runtime is unchanged.
  - **Action:** None.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** The harness now answers the same status, `Allow` header and body as production, through the same helper, and the `admin` handler is not called for those methods; every other method reaches it exactly as before.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: a HEAD request carries no payload bytes.** uWS writes whatever `end()` is handed and SvelteKit renders HEAD as the GET, so a HEAD to a page, an endpoint, the authenticate path's 405, a refused request or the admin lane put bytes after the header block, where a keep-alive client parsed them as the start of the next response.
  - **Affects:** Clients that keep a connection open across a HEAD; the GET to the same target is byte-identical.
  - **Action:** None.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** Status codes are unchanged. A generated error and an admin body still name their size in `Content-Length`, and a page names the length SvelteKit declares. An endpoint that declared none sends no framing header where it used to name the body it wrote, and a HEAD is answered in identity form: the adapter negotiates no encoding for it and adds no `Content-Encoding` or `Vary` of its own, whatever the client offered, while headers the app set ride along as before. `createTestServer` answers its admin lane the same way.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: a 204 carries no Content-Length, and a 304 only the one the app declared.** RFC 9110 forbids the header on a 204 and permits it on a 304 only when it names the 200's content length, so the bodyless responses that ended with a zero (or with `end()`, which writes one) now report none there.
  - **Affects:** Anyone comparing the header set byte for byte, and strict HTTP/1.1 intermediaries; browsers and `fetch` tolerated the zero.
  - **Action:** None.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** uWS emits neither `Content-Length` nor `Transfer-Encoding` when no length is reported, and the exchange still completes, so a request pipelined behind the response is answered as before. `vite dev` already sent none, since Node's HTTP server adds no length to a 204 or 304 of its own.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
- **Fixed: a request that frames its body two ways is refused and its connection closed.** The vendored parser reads the presence of `Transfer-Encoding`, not its value, so `xchunked`, `gzip` and `chunked, chunked` were all decoded as chunked while an intermediary in front read them as something else, which is the disagreement a smuggled request is made of.
  - **Affects:** Deployments behind a proxy or CDN, where the two readings can be made to disagree. A conformant `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` request is served exactly as before, in any capitalisation.
  - **Action:** None.
  - **Requires:** No new dependency or option.
  - **Compatibility:** The refusal is 400 and the connection ends, since the bytes the sender left behind are the ones the two readings disagree about. Every lane refuses a `Transfer-Encoding` naming anything but chunked, the WebSocket handshake included, where `upgrade_rejected_total` gains the reason `ambiguous_framing`. A framing header sent EMPTY or sent TWICE is refused only where the whole header set is read AND acted on, which is the SSR, authenticate, admin and handshake doors; every answer written before such a read serves it, a built asset and a prerendered page among them. That is a measured price rather than an oversight. A refusal that is not about framing, a repeated `Authorization` among them, keeps its connection open as before.
  - **Detail:** [Fixed engineering detail](#fixed).
<!-- consumer-release-summary:end -->

### Added

- **The app-driven topic epoch mint.** The explicit seq lane is
  single-authority per topic, and an app that changes a topic's authority
  had no way to say so: offsets recorded under the old allocator would
  gap-fill from a seq space that no longer continues them, silently
  skipping or duplicating state - the exact failure the epoch machinery
  exists to catch, reachable by a deliberate migration as surely as by a
  relay loss. `platform.bumpTopicEpoch(topic)` mints and installs a fresh
  per-topic generation through the same shared module the confirmed-loss
  drain uses (`mintTopicEpoch`), with a re-roll guard so the mint can never
  equal the value it replaces - a deliberate bump has the current value in
  hand, unlike the loss drain's unknowable client-held one. Worker-local by
  the same design: app code runs on every worker, each mints independently,
  and the equality-only epoch repudiates old offsets everywhere. The
  harness and dev surfaces answer per-topic epochs through the same module
  now, where they previously answered only the process generation.
  `test/topic-epoch-bump.test.js` pins the read-authority change, the u32
  wire domain, and the ack a real client receives after a bump.

- **The send lanes' explicit gap-fill seq.** The resume hook's contract asks
  it to return the highest seq it delivered per topic, but the only primitive
  it had for delivering - `platform.send` - emitted envelopes with no seq
  field, and `sendWire` hardwired the binary frame's seq slot to zero. The
  client's watermark therefore leaned entirely on the returned ceiling; the
  frames themselves said nothing. `options.seq` on both lanes now carries an
  explicit value into the envelope and the seq slot identically, resolved by
  one shared validator (`resolveSendSeq`) on production, `createTestServer`,
  and the Vite dev plugin: number and bigint validate exactly as
  the publish lanes' explicit authority, `false`/`null`/absent leave the
  frame byte-identical to every prior release, and `true` throws its own
  message - the send lanes have no counter to draw, and gap-fill replays
  history that is already accounted, which is why an explicitly-seq'd send
  stays side-effect-free: no counter advance, no max-seen record, no resume
  capture. `sendWireBatch` takes no seq option - one options value cannot be
  one-seq-per-entry, the batch lanes' standing category error - so a seq'd
  replay sends its discrete frames through `sendWire`.
  `test/send-seq.test.js` pins the stamped forms, the refusals, the
  side-effect absence, the binary/JSON parity, and the harness mirror.

- **The static lane's RFC 9110 preconditions.** Mutable entries record their
  file's modification time at index time - the same stat the ETag already
  reads, floored to the whole-second precision HTTP dates carry - and serve
  `Last-Modified` beside the validator; immutable assets keep serving neither,
  their versioned filename being the validator. A pure planner evaluates in
  the RFC's order: `If-Match` first (412 on a miss), `If-Unmodified-Since`
  only in its absence, then `If-None-Match` (now list-form and `*` aware),
  then `If-Modified-Since` only when no entity validator was sent - so a
  failed `If-Match` is never converted into a 304 by a later header.
  `If-Match` matches by opaque equality against any validator the lane issued
  for the asset (identity, brotli, gzip): every validator is weak by
  construction, strict strong comparison would answer 412 to a client echoing
  the exact tag the server handed it, and which representation today's
  request selects says nothing about which one the client holds.
  `If-None-Match` keeps validating the selected representation, as the 304
  always did. An unparseable date is an ignored header, never a refusal. The
  304 carries `Last-Modified` beside the validator set it already named;
  the 412 is minimal. `last-modified` is reserved from `staticHeaders` so a
  configured value cannot displace the real file time.
  `test/static-preconditions.test.js` carries the case table: precedence
  pins, boundary dates at the exact second, list and `*` forms, the
  representation distinction, and the immutable exemption.

- **A subscription-accounting sink that displaces another one now reports
  it.** The sink is one `Symbol.for` slot on `globalThis`, so every copy of
  the module in a worker addresses the same counter, and an install replaced
  whatever was there without a word. Two runtime copies each register at
  module scope; the second takes every delta, and afterwards one counter is
  frozen while the other is charged releases for memberships it never added.
  Those are the two shapes such a deployment reports from the outside: a
  total stuck under its own summed bookkeeping on the displaced side, and a
  total driven negative by unmatched releases on the other. The negative
  always reads exactly `-1`, because `adjustTotalSubscriptions` clamps to
  zero after reporting, so every unmatched release starts from zero again.
  The install now returns whether it displaced a different sink, and the
  handler reports that through the operational channel at `warn`, as
  `ADAPTER-ERR-SUBSCRIPTION-SINK-DISPLACED`. Reported rather than asserted:
  a soft assertion throws under `NODE_ENV=test`, and holding two
  independently built runtimes in one test process is an ordinary thing for
  this suite to do - the condition describes a deployment that carries two
  copies, not a harness that deliberately holds two.
  Clearing the slot to `null` and reinstalling the same function are not
